faq.q1: How much does a website cost?
faq.a1:
€64.99 to set up a one-page website. After that, any work is €34.99 an hour, billed to the nearest 15 minutes. You always get an estimate before we start, so there are no surprise bills.

We offer reduced rates for registered local charities and community groups.

grantsPage.title: Website grants in Ireland: what's actually available
grantsPage.intro: Plenty of agency sites still advertise 50% website grants. Here is the current position, so you can plan your budget with accurate numbers.
grantsPage.warningText1: No work can commence and no payments can be made before receiving your official Letter of Offer.
grantsPage.warningText2: If you pay a deposit or if design/development work starts before your application is approved and the Letter of Offer is issued, that work becomes entirely ineligible for funding.
grantsPage.programsSub: What each Local Enterprise Office (LEO) programme covers, and what it doesn't.
grantsPage.timelineTitle: If you want to apply for a grant
grantsPage.timelineSub: Talk to your LEO first. Don't pay a deposit until you have a Letter of Offer.
grantsPage.westmeathTitle: Based in Co. Westmeath? Apply Locally
grantsPage.westmeathDesc: We are located near Kinnegad, Co. Westmeath. For local clients, we recommend coordinating with the Westmeath Local Enterprise Office (LEO) based in Mullingar.
grantsPage.charityDesc1: We keep some time free each year for discounted or free work for registered charities in the Midlands.
grantsPage.charityDesc2: If your charity needs a new site or needs technical upgrades to accept donations, please reach out directly via the contact form and mention your charity registration details.

pricing.title: Simple, honest pricing
pricing.subtitle: One price to get online, one hourly rate for everything after. No packages to decode.
pricing.note: No monthly fee to us. Your only running cost is your domain name (about €20 a year), paid directly to the registrar in your name. You're never tied in.
faq.a5: Not to us. You pay for your domain name (about €20 a year) directly, in your own name. If you want business email, that's a separate subscription like Google Workspace or Microsoft 365, also in your name.
faq.q6: Can a grant pay for my website?
faq.a6: Probably not for a custom-built site. The Trading Online Voucher closed in December 2024, and the Grow Digital Voucher that replaced it excludes bespoke website development. It can co-fund new software subscriptions and training. Always check with your Local Enterprise Office before paying anyone, as costs incurred before approval can't be claimed.
